
---
title: "OpenCode"
---

[OpenCode](https://opencode.ai/) is an open-source AI coding agent
that runs in the terminal and works directly with local repositories.

## Installation

OpenCode is installed through the `opencode` Ansible role.

```sh
ansible-playbook -i inventory -K playbooks/lab-stack.yml --tags opencode
```

The role also installs CLI tools commonly used when exploring and working with
repositories: `ripgrep`, `fd-find`, `jq`, `gh`, `git-delta`, `fzf`, `bat`,
`ShellCheck`, and `tree`.

The role also installs the [OpenCode Voice plugin](https://github.com/ihxnnxs/opencode-voice)
in the target user's global OpenCode configuration. Restart OpenCode after installation
or an update. On first use, choose a local transcription model; its runtime and model
files are downloaded automatically.

::: {.callout-check}
**✅ Check**

```sh
opencode --version
rg --version
fd --version
jq --version
gh --version
delta --version
fzf --version
bat --version
shellcheck --version
tree --version
```
:::

## Authentication

Authentication is configured manually and is not managed by Ansible.

Launch OpenCode:

```sh
opencode
```

Inside OpenCode, enter `/connect`, select a provider, and follow its authentication
prompts. Providers may use an API key or an account sign-in flow. Then run `/models`
to select an available model. See the [OpenCode provider guide](https://opencode.ai/docs/providers/)
for provider-specific instructions.

OpenCode stores credentials locally; do not commit credentials or local authentication
files to this repository.

## Voice input

Press `Ctrl+R` to start recording, then press it again to stop and transcribe into the
prompt. Use `/voice-settings` to change the model, microphone, language, and recording
hotkey. Voice transcription runs locally.

## Working with repositories

Launch OpenCode from the repository root:

```sh
cd ~/repos/colrev
opencode
```

Use Plan mode to review proposed changes before allowing edits.

Review modifications using:

```bash
git status
git diff
```

## Best practices and useful links

Start OpenCode from the repository root so it can read the project guidance in
`AGENTS.md`. If the project does not have one, run `/init`, review the generated
instructions, and commit the file with the project.

For larger changes, use Plan mode (`Tab`) to agree on an approach before editing.
Before committing, review `git status` and `git diff` and run the project's relevant
checks.

Useful references:

- [OpenCode rules and `AGENTS.md`](https://opencode.ai/docs/rules/)
- [OpenCode tools and permissions](https://opencode.ai/docs/tools/)
- [Workstation setup and verification](install_configuration.qmd)

## Updates

OpenCode is managed by the workstation Ansible role.
The regular configuration run ensures it is installed.

To upgrade OpenCode explicitly:

```sh
opencode upgrade
```

Restart OpenCode after upgrading so it reloads the installed CLI and plugins.
